## Helping Customers Move from Urgency to Action


As organizations put AI agents to work, they’re giving more identities access to sensitive information, critical systems and the ability to take action across the business. Each new agent deployment involves decisions about how much access the agent needs — and how to control that access.


[AI adds a new layer of security complexity](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/2025/09/securing-the-future-of-ai/) for customers already working to manage the permissions employees and machines hold. Excessive privileges, exposed credentials and forgotten accounts create opportunities for malicious actors both inside and outside the organization, and AI can help them exploit those weaknesses faster.[In a recent Unit 42 investigation](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cyber-attack-inside-a-unit-42-investigation/) , an attacker used AI agents to breach an enterprise network in less than 10 hours — an intrusion that would typically take human operators about two weeks. Along the way, the agents exploited exposed credentials to gain privileged access and steal cloud keys.


Customers need to bring existing access under control while establishing guardrails for AI initiatives. When separate tools and teams manage different parts of identity security, it becomes harder to see the full picture and act on it consistently. That makes a unified approach to identity security increasingly essential — one enabled by[Idira™](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/idira) , the Palo Alto Networks next-generation identity security platform.


[In a previous post](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/2026/06/a-defining-moment-in-identity-security/) , I highlighted the opportunity for Palo Alto Networks and our partners to seize a defining moment in identity security and help customers rethink identity as a foundation of security for the AI enterprise. (You can explore that connection further in[this video](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/content/dam/pan/en_US/partners/videos/identity-security-enhances-partner-program-english.mp4) and[blog post](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/identity-security/frontier-ai-identity-security-90-day-plan/) .) Our challenge, and opportunity, is to help customers understand where their current approach leaves them exposed and take practical steps to close those gaps.


For partners, this creates a full services lifecycle: assessing identity risk, implementing modern privilege controls and managing governance over time. Each stage is a natural engagement, and together they give partners a path to grow with customers as their AI use expands.


## Recognizing Why Identity Security Can’t Wait


When organizations adopt AI, they’re introducing agents into environments where employees may already have more access than they need, and machine accounts may still hold permissions from projects that ended months ago. Adding agents without addressing those gaps can compound the risk.


Partners can help customers connect their AI plans with the access decisions those initiatives require. A customer may be focused on what a new agent can accomplish, but they also need to understand what they’re authorizing it to do. An agent acting for an employee should stay within the access appropriate to that person and task. Establishing those boundaries at the outset puts customers in a better position to expand AI use securely.


Those access decisions also matter when something goes wrong. If an identity is compromised, the permissions attached to it can determine how far an attacker gets and what damage they can cause. Reducing unnecessary access — and limiting how long elevated permissions remain available — removes some of the fuel that allows an attack to spread.


[Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report](https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/reports/2026-dbir-data-breach-investigations-report.pdf) reinforces that point: Privilege management could help mitigate roughly 65% of the privilege escalation and credential access techniques examined in its analysis. Controlling permissions can make a meaningful difference in how far an attacker gets.


Network, cloud and endpoint defenses remain essential, of course. But[identity security](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/cyberpedia/what-is-identity-security) reinforces those protections by limiting what an attacker can do with a compromised account or credential.[The 2026 Global Incident Response Report](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/resources/research/unit-42-incident-response-report) from Unit 42 underscores its importance, finding that identity weaknesses played a material role in nearly 90% of investigations over the past year. Strong identity security can help stop an initial intrusion from escalating into data theft, disrupted operations or lasting damage to customer trust.


## Rethinking Who and What Holds Privilege


Ask customers who their privileged users are and, for many, IT administrators will likely come to mind first. But access to sensitive information and important business systems extends to users across the organization.


Think about the access people need to do their jobs. Someone in marketing may manage the company’s social accounts, while a colleague in sales can download customer records and confidential pricing agreements. Neither may be considered a privileged user, yet a compromised account could damage the company’s reputation or expose sensitive customer information, confidential business plans or intellectual property. Now consider a developer giving an AI agent access to code repositories. That agent is taking on access that carries its own risks and needs appropriate controls.


Examining privileged access in these everyday activities can bring more people into the identity security discussion. Application owners, development teams and business leaders can help identify which permissions are necessary and where tighter controls could interfere with day-to-day work. For example, cumbersome access processes can encourage developers to find workarounds. Making appropriate access easier to obtain while ensuring elevated permissions expire when no longer needed can reduce exposure without slowing development.


## Keeping Access Aligned with Business Needs


Access is often granted to meet an immediate business need. But without continuous oversight, permissions, credentials and connections can persist long after that need has passed. This accumulated “identity debt” can leave organizations exposed in ways they no longer recognize or fully understand.


Consider a partner implementing a new application for a customer. The project may require temporary access and connections between systems. Before the project ends, the partner should work with the customer to determine which permissions remain necessary, who will own the associated identities and how access will be reviewed and revoked over time.


According to our[2026 Identity Security Landscape report](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/idira/idira-identity-security-landscape) , machine identities, including AI agents, now outnumber human identities 109 to 1. These identities often retain access they no longer need. Securing them requires different controls than securing human users, but a unified approach helps customers manage permissions across all identities and adjust them as business needs change.


## Enabling Continuous Discovery, Control and Governance of Identities Through Platformization


Partners can help customers get started with implementing identity security by focusing on three priorities:


- **Discover identity risk.** Help customers see which human, machine and AI agent identities have access, what privileges they hold and where credentials may be exposed. AI-driven discovery and analytics can surface risks that are difficult to find manually. Identifying excessive privileges and standing access gives partners a practical starting point for a customer assessment.
- **Control every privilege.** Partners can help customers rethink how much access they leave in place between tasks. Modern privileged access management (PAM) from Idira™ supports a move toward zero standing privilege for every identity, with elevated permissions granted just in time to perform authorized work. Organizations can give people the access they need while reducing the risk that comes with leaving those permissions always on.
- **Automate governance.** Keep permissions aligned with changing roles, projects and business needs. CORA AI, built into Idira, helps automate how access is granted, reviewed and removed across the identity lifecycle. That helps businesses keep pace with change, reduce administrative work and support compliance.


These activities need to work together. Once a customer identifies excessive access, they need to adjust permissions and keep them aligned with evolving business needs. Continuous discovery helps them spot new risks along the way. Idira™ simplifies this process by bringing discovery, privilege controls and governance together across human, machine and agentic identities.


## Bringing Identity Security into Customer Transformation Plans


Partners are well-positioned to connect identity security to the transformations customers already have underway. A cloud migration, application modernization project or AI deployment is a chance to help customers evaluate who and what needs access and how to manage that access from the start.


Some customers will need an assessment and a road map. Others will seek implementation expertise, privilege modernization or ongoing operational support. Understanding those needs gives partners a starting point to expand their services and help customers make identity security part of their broader security strategy.[For managed security service providers (MSSPs)](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/partners/managed-security-service-providers) , Idira offers an opportunity to build managed identity security services on a unified platform, with native identity posture management and threat detection capabilities, rather than stitching together separate tools.


Our customers are making many critical decisions about AI and access now. We can help them ask the right questions before granting permissions, put processes in place to revisit those decisions as their business changes and make identity security part of how they operate, with access that serves a clear purpose and is removed when that purpose ends.

## Key Takeaways


- AI makes identity security more urgent by expanding access and accelerating attacks.
- A unified platform connects discovery, privilege controls and governance to secure every identity - human, machine and AI agent.
